newsitem.title: USA: ITT sees potential suitors for Europe hotels.
newsitem.headline: ITT sees potential suitors for Europe hotels.

text.p: Hotel and casino giant ITT Corp., fighting a $6.5 billion hostile takeover from Hilton Hotels Corp., said Wednesday it has been approached about selling its stake in a group of European luxury hotels.
The company, owner of Sheraton hotels and Caesars World casinos, said the potential suitors have expressed interest in ITT's full 70 percent stake in Cigahotels SpA, as well as portions of it.
"ITT is considering all of its options regarding its position in Ciga, as well as other hotels, taking into account the best interests of its shareholders," the company said in a news release.
ITT bought the stake in Ciga, a group of about 30 hotels, in 1994 as part of a geographical expansion. Public shareholders own the rest of the company.
Spokesman James Gallagher declined to identify the potential suitors or which hotels are being considered.
"All we are saying is that we have been approached. We are examining the expressions of interest," he said.
Hilton disputed ITT's contention that it is looking out for its shareholders.
"If they were genuinely considering the best interest of their shareholders, what they'd be doing is talking to us," spokesman Marc Grossman said.
The Ciga properties are the latest assets being considered for sale by ITT, which also has received buying interest for its luxury St. Regis hotel in New York and Phoenician hotel in Arizona.
The hotel and casino giant also is in talks to sell its Desert Inn and Tunica casino properties.

ITT has sold several holdings since Hilton launched the bid in January, including its stake in Madison Square Garden. The company has said it will consider selling non-core assets in an attempt to focus on its Sheraton and Caesars World businesses.
The stock of ITT edgd up 12.5 cents to $59.375 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
